subject: Clarifying output title vs. license, training authorization & feedback permit — next steps
messages:
From: Dana Brooks <dana@bluearc.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@bluearc.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines — IP and feedback license

Markus,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal and product teams reviewed and flagged three areas we need to resolve before procurement can move forward: output ownership (your current template looks like an assignment of "customer-created outputs" which raises productization concerns), model training/data use (we need clarity about whether BlueArc data or outputs can be used to improve or retrain models), and the feedback license (we can provide product feedback but cannot give a perpetual right to use it for training without controls).

Quick summary of our asks in the attached redlines (BlueArc_MSA_Redlines_v2.pdf):
- Output: Prefer a scoped, non-exclusive license for outputs used in our product; not an assignment.
- Training: Opt-in model retrain only with an explicit opt-in checkbox per environment; require anonymization and a deletion window.
- Feedback license: Limited to internal model tuning and non-commercial research; delete upon request.

Can Redwood propose specific clause language that preserves our need to productize derivative features while giving Redwood operational flexibility to improve models? We can do a short call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Regards,
Dana Brooks
Head of Platform Legal
BlueArc Systems

Attachments: BlueArc_MSA_Redlines_v2.pdf (annotated MSA)

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — IP and feedback license

Team — forwarding BlueArc's redlines (attached). Key asks: scoped license for outputs, opt-in training, and narrow feedback rights. Procurement wants concrete clause language; product wants to know if we can ship a runtime-only license for outputs (no assignment).

Proposed internal plan:
1) Laura: draft two short clause options (A = runtime license + attribution; B = narrowly scoped assignment for clearly defined "customer product outputs") with fallback language.
2) Priyom/Karthik: confirm whether runtime-only license will break any existing telemetry/monetization features; flag operational constraints (KV cache/logs retention).
3) Neha: prepare evidence pack for BlueArc (SOC2 excerpts + telemetry retention policy) for procurement.
4) I will propose language to BlueArc and offer a short call Wed 2pm PT.

Please add estimated turnaround (hours) and any hard stop items. I attached a draft of our suggested wording (Redline_Suggested_Clauses.docx).

Thanks — Markus
VP, Customer & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redline_Suggested_Clauses.docx (first-pass language)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines — IP and feedback license

Markus / all — reviewed BlueArc's asks. High level thoughts and two pragmatic clause options to test in negotiations:

Summary (short):
- Output ownership: avoid broad assignment. Offer a narrow, transferable license for "Customer Outputs" defined as unmodified content generated from Customer-provided prompts and data; allow Customer to productize but exclude using Customer Outputs to train backbone models without opt-in.
- Training/data use: propose an opt-in "Model Improvement" toggle. If enabled, data is pseudonymized, stored for a defined retention (e.g., 90 days), and used only to improve Redwood inference layers (not sold or re-licensed).
- Feedback license: limited, non-exclusive, revocable license for feedback used to improve services; Redwood will not use feedback to create a competing product or for commercial model resale.

Suggested language (very condensed for email):
Option A (preferred):
- "Customer Outputs" remain Customer's content. Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Customer Outputs for the limited purpose of providing and improving the Service, excluding training of Redwood base models except where Customer has explicitly opted in via the Order Form. Redwood will not claim ownership of Customer Outputs.

Option B (fallback for high-risk customers):
- "Customer Outputs" ownership transfers only for specifically identified artifacts listed in Exhibit A; otherwise Redwood receives the same limited license as above. Exhibit A must be mutually agreed and narrow.

Telemetry/ops constraints to call out to product/ops:
- We need to confirm anonymization threshold (PII scrub + token-level hash) and retention/erasement workflow; ops must confirm feasibility for 90-day window.

Next steps:
- I can produce redline snippets for both options (A and B) in ~4 business hours.
- If we present Option A plus an explicit opt-in toggle for retrain, that's likely to resolve most procurement objections.

I'll attach short redline snippets in the Drive link and add comments on the two clauses.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (Draft clauses uploaded to internal Drive link)

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Dana Brooks <dana@bluearc.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, procurement@bluearc.com
Date: 2026-08-24T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — IP and feedback license

Dana — thanks for the clear redlines and context. Quick reply with a path forward so procurement can keep moving: 

Proposal (high level):
- Output: Redwood will not take broad assignment. We propose Option A (non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license) with an explicit carveout: Redwood will not use "Customer Outputs" to retrain backbone models unless BlueArc opts in via the Order Form. If BlueArc needs full assignment for a narrow set of artifacts, we can support that only if the artifacts are enumerated in Exhibit A and mutually approved.
- Training: add an opt-in "Model Improvement" checkbox in the Order Form. If checked, data is pseudonymized, retained for 90 days only, and used solely for service improvement (no resale). Ops will provide a short runbook describing anonymization and deletion steps before signing.
- Feedback: Redwood requests a limited, revocable license to use feedback for internal model tuning and service improvement; feedback will be excluded from any commercial model redistribution and will be removed on request.

Action items: 
- Laura: please send the two redline snippets (Option A + Exhibit A fallback) by EOD PT today so we can share formal wording.
- Priyom/Karthik: confirm within 24 hours whether the 90-day pseudonymized retention + deletion workflow is operationally feasible. If there are constraints, please specify them.
- Dana / BlueArc procurement: please confirm whether the Order Form opt-in checkbox is acceptable and whether you'd like the Exhibit A route for any specific artifacts. If helpful we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow 2pm PT to run through the exact clause text.

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. Hoping this balances productization needs with your data protections.

Markus Klein
VP, Customer & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

References: Redline_Suggested_Clauses.docx (internal draft), BlueArc_MSA_Redlines_v2.pdf (your annotated file)
thread_summary: External (BlueArc) flagged output assignment, training opt-in, and feedback license. Markus coordinated internal counsel and product; Laura proposed Option A (runtime license + opt-in retrain) with Exhibit A fallback. Markus proposed presenting Option A + Order Form opt-in and requested operational confirmation on pseudonymization and 90-day retention. Awaiting Laura's redlines and ops feasibility confirmation.
